biscuit.prep: Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
biscuit.cook: Place the biscuits close together on the sheet (they rise taller when their sides touch). Bake at {temp} for {time}, until tall and golden brown.
biscuit.check: The tops should be deep golden and the biscuits should feel light for their size.
notes: @butter: A very hot oven makes the butter steam, creating flaky layers.
Serve warm - biscuits are best within an hour of baking.

biscuit.prep: Line the basket with perforated air fryer parchment, or lightly grease it.
biscuit.cook: Place 3-4 biscuits in the basket so their sides just touch. Air fry at {temp} for {time}, until tall and golden.
biscuit.check: The tops should be golden and the biscuits should feel light for their size. If they brown too fast, cover loosely with foil.
notes: Air fryers vary a lot - start checking at the early end of the range.
Do not crowd the basket - biscuits need room to rise.

recipes.name: Buttermilk Biscuits
recipes.description: Tall, flaky biscuits with buttery layers.

yield.note: Cut with a 6 cm (2 1/2 in) cutter.

less.note: Biscuits are barely sweet - only a tablespoon of sugar - so halving it makes almost no difference.

steps.title: Mix Dry Ingredients
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the dry ingredients.

steps.title: Cut In the {^butter|Butter}
steps.text: Rub or grate the {@butter|very cold butter} into the flour until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs with pea-sized pieces.

steps.title: Add the {^buttermilk|Buttermilk}
steps.text: Pour in the {#buttermilk|buttermilk} and stir with a fork until a shaggy dough forms. Do not overmix.

steps.title: Fold and Cut
steps.text: Turn the dough onto a floured surface and pat it to about 2.5 cm (1 in) thick. Fold it in thirds twice for flaky layers, pat out again and cut straight down with a floured cutter - do not twist.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Brush the warm biscuits with a little {@butter|melted butter} if you like.

tips: @butter,buttermilk: Keep the butter and buttermilk very cold.
Press the cutter straight down - twisting seals the edges and stops the rise.
Pat out and cut quickly; overworked dough makes tough biscuits.

recipes.name: Cheddar Biscuits
recipes.description: Savory, cheesy biscuits with a hint of garlic.

yield.note: Cut with a 6 cm (2 1/2 in) cutter.

less.note: These savory biscuits use just 2 teaspoons of sugar, so halving it makes almost no difference.

steps.title: Mix Dry Ingredients
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the {L|=flour;#baking_powder|baking powder;=salt;#garlic_powder|garlic powder;#granulated_sugar|sugar}.

steps.title: Cut In the {^butter|Butter}
steps.text: Rub or grate the {@butter|very cold butter} into the flour until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs with pea-sized pieces. Stir in the cheddar.

steps.title: Add the {^buttermilk|Buttermilk}
steps.text: Pour in the {#buttermilk|buttermilk} and stir with a fork until a shaggy dough forms. Do not overmix.

steps.title: Fold and Cut
steps.text: Turn the dough onto a floured surface and pat it to about 2.5 cm (1 in) thick. Fold it in thirds once, pat out again and cut straight down with a floured cutter - do not twist.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Brush the warm biscuits with {@butter|melted butter} if you like.

tips: Use freshly shredded cheddar - pre-shredded cheese has anti-caking powder that dries the dough.
@butter,buttermilk: Keep the butter and buttermilk very cold.
@butter: A garlic-butter brush right out of the oven makes them irresistible.
